summary: Bibb County tower on the Talladega National Forest, built in 1937 to protect Resettlement Administration land; run by the Forest Service and registered in 2011.

notes_for_editor: Built year (1937), agency, registration and elevation match the record. Staffing, access and any post-2012 status not found; the newest source is the 2012 decision, so 'standing' is supported only through 2012. Record elevation 173.4 m matches the Register's 173 m. The NHLR attributes the land to the Resettlement Administration, while the Forest Service history describes the Oakmulgee purchase unit as created in 1935 by a national forest commission. These do not contradict each other, but the land history is not fully reconciled. The Forest Service history gives the Pondville name as a former working circle, not the tower's own history, so it is used only for the 1936 forest creation date.
